symptom: a null LITERAL operand on an ordering/substring comparison raised a raw ORM error ('Cannot use None as a query value') instead of a clean two-valued FALSE
`x = null` / `x != null` lowered to IS NULL / IS NOT NULL (a Django field=None artifact) instead of the two-valued genuine-FALSE the spec mandates — a silent wrong answer on the null boundary
single-hop `MATCH (a)-[:E]->(b) RETURN a.x` fell to the ENVELOPE dispatch which silently ignored the projection (rows=None) — the accept-and-drop class
bare-var `RETURN a, b` over `-[]->` dropped the anonymous connecting edge from the envelope (only NAMED edges were collected)
the reference oracle's per-clause union scoping substituted TRUE for an unbound-variable leaf then evaluated it, so NOT over that leaf wrongly emptied the arm — a bug in the checker itself

the single-hop hub-and-spoke / edge-type-scan dispatch honored only an entity_id anchor and silently dropped every other WHERE predicate; fixed by collapsing all single-hop dispatch through the WHERE-applying chain path

a multi-hop WHERE on a node beyond the root edge, applied as a separate .filter() from the structural chain filters, spawned a duplicate edges_out join carrying no edge-type filter — so the chain returned far nodes reached by the WRONG edge type and inflated COUNT

`!=` or `NOT (...)` on a far node lowered to ~Q over a multi-valued reverse-FK path, which Django compiles as an existential anti-join subquery — 'operator does not exist: bigint = uuid' crash + wrong (per-pattern) semantics; now cleanly rejected
